title: A Orchard for the Tide
premise: Sebastian Galloway inherited a failing orchard-vineyard and crushing debts, and when the town's anonymous pen-pal program pairs him with the one woman who wants his land foreclosed, neither realizes it at first. Marisol Vega, the bank's sharp new appraiser, falls for the stranger in her letters while warring with him in person, until the truth surfaces and both must choose between pride and honesty. As the last harvest approaches and the foreclosure deadline looms, Sebastian risks everything on one honest letter, and Marisol must decide whether to save the orchard or her career. They end by planting a new graft together — the orchard survives, smaller but theirs.
about_author: Xanthe Okafor is a former agricultural loan officer who traded spreadsheets for storytelling after a decade of watching people fight for their land. She writes romances rooted in soil, debt, and the stubborn arithmetic of second chances from a farmhouse on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Soil
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He walks the frost-bitten rows of Galloway Orchard, tallying debts his father left behind and the foreclosure notice pinned to the barn door. Emotional beat: weary defiance — he'll sell everything except the oldest trees.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. New to town as the bank's appraiser, she signs up for the library's anonymous pen-pal program to feel less like an outsider. Her first letter goes out; so does Sebastian's, entered by his meddling aunt. Beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Enemies at the Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marisol arrives to appraise the orchard; Sebastian recognizes the bank's letterhead and slams the gate. Their first meeting is pure friction over dead vines and unpaid interest. Beat: mutual contempt with an unwanted flicker of respect.

chapters.title: Letters Without Faces
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Both write their anonymous letters that night — Sebastian venting about 'the vulture from the bank,' Marisol confessing she hates what her job sometimes requires. Neither knows who they're writing. Beat: ironic tenderness.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She walks the property alone, finding beauty the numbers can't hold: a child's swing, grafts in her grandfather's handwriting style. Her report draft comes back lower than her heart wants. Beat: guilt taking root.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A storm traps Marisol at the orchard after the last train leaves; he grudgingly offers cider and the spare room. They talk until midnight without armor. Beat: the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: What the Letters Reveal
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pen-pal exchange deepens — each unknowingly describes the other's storm night. Marisol realizes her correspondent might be Sebastian; Sebastian suspects nothing yet. Beat: vertigo of almost-knowing.

chapters.title: The Deadline Letter
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The bank sets a final date: pay or forfeit in six weeks. She must deliver the news herself and watches hope die on his face. Beat: complicity — she has become the villain in someone's story.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Desperate for labor, he hires Marisol's weekend help when no one else shows. Working side by side, their bodies learn a rhythm their words refuse. Beat: reluctant partnership warming into something else.

chapters.title: The Aunt's Interference
chapters.summary: Supporting POV (Aunt Ruth). Ruth, who enrolled them both, discovers the pen-pals' identities and says nothing, arranging instead a shared delivery of two identical letters. Beat: mischievous hope, and dread of the fallout.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the harvest festival, nearly- confessions collide; Marisol almost tells him she's his pen-pal, then learns he plans to expose the bank's predatory terms using her own reports. Beat: betrayal before betrayal happens.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He finds her unsent letter in the barn — her handwriting matching months of correspondence. Confrontation in the rain: every tender word now reads as espionage. Beat: heartbreak weaponized.

chapters.title: Silence Between Rows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She withdraws the letters, requests reassignment, and drafts her resignation. But she also quietly flags the bank's irregular fees to a state regulator. Beat: choosing conscience over safety.

chapters.title: The Regulator's Visit
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. State auditors arrive — Marisol's anonymous complaint bought him time. He realizes what she sacrificed and that his anger may have cost him the truest thing he's had. Beat: regret sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: One Last Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He writes her honestly, unsigned no more, and mails it to the bank itself. Beat: vulnerability as courage — laying his heart out where her career can crush it.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She reads his letter in front of her supervisor, who demands she recant or resign. She resigns. Beat: liberation with a cliff-edge — no job, no plan, one address in her pocket.

chapters.title: The Bank's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The bank accelerates the foreclosure out of spite; auction set for dawn after the final harvest. Both race the clock — Sebastian to bring in the crop, Marisol to prove the fraud. Beat: rising desperation.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She boards the train out, then steps off at the last second, arriving soaked at the orchard gate as the storm returns. 'Let me stay.' Beat: surrender to love over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Frost Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Climax. Together they fight an all-night frost — smudge pots, wind machines, prayer — saving the crop that funds the redemption bid. In the ash-light of dawn they finally say everything aloud. Beat: triumph forged in exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At auction, the crop money plus evidence of fraudulent fees forces the bank to settle: the debt restructured, the orchard saved at a fraction of the price. Beat: justice arriving quiet and earned.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Spring. She plants a new apple variety grafted onto old rootstock — her name beside his in the ledger. The pen-pal letters are framed above the mantel. Beat: identity remade, together.

chapters.title: An Orchard for the Tide
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing. One year later, they host the town's next pen-pal reveal night on the hillside as the tide turns below. Second chances, they've learned, are for people brave enough to be honest in time. Beat: full-circle peace.
